targets.title: Can conformity bias be observed in questions whose answers are objectively fixed?
targets.evidence_quote:
We conducted two replications of Fujikawa et al. (2024)
in which one of the four response patterns of hypothetical
nine other participants was randomly presented (betweenparticipants design) for students (Exp. 1) and crowd
workers (Exp. 2).
targets.outcome_quote:
The results showed
a conformist bias for most objective questions, but a
nonconformist-bias for attitude questions. The finding of
nonconformist-bias for attitude questions is consistent with
the findings of Eriksson and Coultas (2009), but the finding
that conformist bias was only observed for objective
questions differs from the findings of Fujikawa et al. (2024).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original showed bias for both objective and attitude questions. Present experiments retain objective-question bias but explicitly contrast absence of attitude-question bias with original. Eriksson and Coultas supply the preceding chain study and procedure, not an additional direct target. No overall verdict overrides these comparisons.

reasoning: Title, DOI, authors, six-page article and references verified. Two fresh samples test the named earlier published Fujikawa paper using a between-participants design.
